title: The twin contract: the system and an AI-first agent on one step, their differences, and where each approach is best
request: Phase 3 of the owner's plan: at every step of DCLab, see at the same time how Claude solves it as an AI-first agent and how the current system does, with the differences, everything kept, and learn where Claude, the software or the two together are best.
spec: dclab_core twin (TwinStep v1, TwinMatrix v1, the step catalogue with a step for every ledger point, compare, judge, effectiveness, twin_rule_v1) and adapters main_product_twin (the main product's rule-and-Jev pairs as twin steps).
plan: One input per step: its fingerprint on the step and on both answers, so a difference is a difference of approach.
Every field of a step is compared by a declared kind (equal, set, ranked, numeric, text by key terms, mapping), and judged against a truth with its source.
The rule that says where each approach is best is in code before any run: software, software reviewed by the AI, the AI checked by the software, the AI, undecided; ties go to the software.
The main product already pairs a rule and Jev on each governed question: read those rows as twin steps.

decisions.decision: The differences and the verdict are computed by the contract, never written by a caller.
decisions.why: A stored verdict that disagrees with its answers would let the matrix count a step for the wrong arm; recomputing on read makes a tampered or stale record fail.

decisions.decision: The AI alone is measured with the system's answer shown where the AI gave none.
decisions.why: That is what a product shows when a model fails or abstains; crediting such fallbacks to the validator would call a step validator-checked when no validator ran.

decisions.decision: The margin is counted in whole judged steps.
decisions.why: A fixed rule must give the same mode for the same lead whatever the base rate; a float sum of shares does not.

decisions.decision: A text answer is right when it holds enough of the truth's key terms; two texts are the same by the overlap of both.
decisions.why: A correct, longer answer must not be judged wrong for saying more, while two arms that say different things must still differ.

decisions.decision: The A6.6 and A6.7 twin runs of the branch sft-factory-all-stages are brought onto main in 25.2 and 25.3, not merged.
decisions.why: The branch left main 114 commits earlier and rests on the A6.5 decision samples, which main replaced with the ledger.

change: dclab_core/twin.py (new), dclab_core/adapters/main_product_twin.py (new), dclab_core/adapters/conformance.py (the adapter and the two contracts), dclab_core/contracts.py (registered), schemas and baselines, version 0.56.0 and its changelog, scripts/core_wheel_check.py, tests/test_twin_steps.py (new), tests/test_conformance.py (phase 3 sections, six contracts read from rows), docs/guides/PHASE3_AI_FIRST_PLAN.md (new), docs/guides/CORE_INTEGRATION.md.

findings.defect: The conformance gate failed: the two new contracts had no adapter and no reason.
findings.scenario: make check-quick runs the conformance test: contract twin_step has no adapter and no reason.
findings.cause: The contracts were registered in CONTRACTS but not in the conformance tables.
findings.fix: The adapter module is in ADAPTERS, twin_step names its reader and is a contract read from rows, twin_matrix is library output.

findings.defect: The rule's margin moved with the base rate through float rounding.
findings.scenario: Ten judged steps and a lead of one step: the system at two and the AI at three gave software, the system at seven and the AI at eight gave the AI.
findings.cause: The shares were added as floats: two tenths plus one tenth is a little more than three tenths.
findings.fix: The margin is compared in whole steps with a small tolerance.

findings.defect: A stored step's differences and verdict were trusted; their defaults meant the arms agreed and nothing was judged.
findings.scenario: A step built without the helper, with different packs and a truth, counted as an agreement and unjudged; an edited winner was read back as written.
findings.cause: Derived fields were ordinary fields with defaults.
findings.fix: The validator computes both from the answers and the truth and refuses a stored value that differs.

findings.defect: An empty input fingerprint was accepted.
findings.scenario: A step and both arms with an empty fingerprint validated, so two inputs could not be told apart.
findings.cause: The field had only a length limit.
findings.fix: The step's fingerprint must be a SHA-256 in hex; the helper documents that an arm without one is vouched for by the host.

findings.defect: Persian text always compared as the same.
findings.scenario: The truth and one arm said customer churn in Persian, the other arm said fraud: both arms were judged right.
findings.cause: Key terms kept only Latin letters and digits, and two empty term sets counted as the same.
findings.fix: Terms are words of any script, casefolded; with no terms the stripped texts must be equal.

findings.defect: Sets and orders of records compared by their key order, and a flag equalled a number.
findings.scenario: The same workflow step written with its keys in another order differed; true equalled one.
findings.cause: Items were compared by their text form and booleans compared as numbers.
findings.fix: Every value is put in a canonical form (strings casefolded, keys sorted, all the way down) and a flag never equals a number.

findings.defect: The AI checked by the software was credited for falling back where the AI failed, with no validator.
findings.scenario: Twelve steps, the AI right on nine and failing on three where the system was right, no validator: the mode said the validator helped.
findings.cause: The checked count used the system's answer for any step the AI did not answer, while the AI alone counted those as wrong.
findings.fix: The AI alone also shows the system's answer where it gave none; the checked mode needs the validator to add right answers beyond that.

findings.defect: Review precision counted disagreements on fields no truth judged.
findings.scenario: The truth only on the identifiers, the arms agreeing on them and differing on the time column: counted as a disagreement.
findings.fix: A disagreement counts only on a field the verdict judges.

findings.defect: The adapter recorded Jev's abstain as a wrong answer.
findings.scenario: An answer outside the acting band became an answered arm with no value: a disagreement and an AI error, with no failure counted.
findings.cause: The banded value was used without reading the row's agreement.
findings.fix: An answer outside the band, or a row marked abstain, is an abstained arm.

findings.defect: Which label became the truth depended on the rows' order, and one broken chain failed the whole batch.
findings.scenario: An answer with two labels in two orders gave two different winners; a second label without its first raised for every step.
findings.cause: Each label overwrote the last, and the reader's error was not caught per row.
findings.fix: The label of the highest version is the truth; a label whose chain is not in the rows is left out and its decision stays unjudged.

findings.defect: Nothing stopped a table's rows from entering a twin record.
findings.scenario: An input summary of five hundred records with e-mails and amounts was accepted.
findings.cause: The answers, the truth and the summary were open JSON with no bounds, unlike the ledger's state.
findings.fix: Answers and truths are bounded in depth, list length and string length; a summary holds only names and counts; a decision step's answers have their point's shape.

findings.defect: The median cost left out an arm that spent and then failed.
findings.scenario: A capped AI arm that spent showed no cost, understating what the AI costs.
findings.cause: Only answered arms entered the median.
findings.fix: Every arm that was not skipped enters the cost median.

findings.defect: A long reply made the step impossible to record.
findings.scenario: A reply over the text limit, or more reasons or tool calls than allowed, raised instead of being kept.
findings.cause: The trimming ran after the length checks.
findings.fix: A validator before the checks cuts the text and the lists and records how much it dropped.

findings.defect: A correct, longer text answer was judged wrong.
findings.scenario: The truth churn against an answer that the customer churns within a month: judged wrong.
findings.cause: Judging used the symmetric overlap of the two texts, with no plural folding.
findings.fix: Judging a text asks how much of the truth's terms the answer holds; a plural's s is folded.

findings.defect: A test expected two texts that say the same to differ.
findings.scenario: Whether the customer churns soon against will the customer churn soon: asserted to differ.
findings.cause: The test's expectation was wrong, not the comparison.
findings.fix: The test asserts they are the same.

findings.defect: The first plan built a second twin beside one already written on another branch.
findings.scenario: The owner pasted the status of the twin runs built on the branch sft-factory-all-stages.
findings.cause: That branch had never been merged and the plan read only main.
findings.fix: The plan brings the branch's lanes and design monitor onto main in 25.2 and 25.3, adapted to the ledger and the native transport.

outcome: The contract and its rule are in the library with the main product's adapter; nothing writes twin steps yet.
lessons: A derived field in a stored contract is computed on read, never trusted.
Count margins in whole cases, not in float shares.
Look for unmerged branches before planning a feature the owner may have asked for before.
risks: Text comparison by key terms is crude for long free answers; the judged steps should prefer coded fields.
